meta.title: Case classification and knowledge: where we started and what we built
meta.subtitle: Help desk email cases get a case type and land in the right queue. First a Prompt Builder template picked the type. Then Einstein Case Classification took over, and Knowledge migrated from OneNote feeds article recommendations.

views.title: First iteration: Prompt Builder classifier
views.intro: A record-triggered flow sent each new case to a Prompt Builder template. The template scored it against 12 case types and returned JSON. An Apex class read that JSON and set Case Type, and routing did the rest.

steps.text: The flow sends the case details to a Prompt Builder template, which assesses them against 12 case types and returns JSON.

steps.title: Apex updates the case
steps.text: An Apex class reads the JSON and sets Case Type on the record.

steps.text: Existing routing sends the case to the queue for its case type.

groups.label: Inside Salesforce: everything here runs on the Case object

views.title: What we built: Einstein Case Classification and Knowledge
views.intro: Everything from classification to the technician's work happens in Salesforce, on the Case object. Einstein Case Classification replaced the prompt: it predicts Case Type from 10 fields on the Case, and the same routing sends it to a queue. Help desk technicians pick up the Case in Salesforce, where Einstein Article Recommendations suggests articles from Knowledge migrated out of OneNote.

steps.text: The same downstream routing sends the Case to the queue for its type, and a help desk technician picks it up and works it in Salesforce.

steps.text: The same Knowledge can be brought into Data Cloud to ground Agentforce agents that answer questions.

cards.title: Live
cards.text: Einstein Case Classification and Article Recommendations live in Fabrikam's production org on Knowledge migrated into Salesforce, rolling out desk by desk.

cards.title: Why we moved off the prompt
cards.text: The Prompt Builder classifier worked, right 70% or more of the time, but every case cost Einstein requests and flex credits, and Fabrikam wanted a predictive model it could keep current as queues change.

cards.title: Future option
cards.text: Knowledge in Data Cloud to ground Agentforce agents, once Fabrikam decides to take on agentic work.
